held_out_evaluation.batch: actual per-trial microbatch from frozen config
held_out_evaluation.comparison_limit: Do not divide model time by the no-NLC row time or claim isolated baseline speed/VRAM from these fields.
held_out_evaluation.no_NLC_rows: no-NLC shares the first candidate evaluation loop for each dataset. Its time and peak allocation are copied from that coupled loop, include candidate inference, and are not isolated no-NLC latency or VRAM.
held_out_evaluation.scope: after checkpoint/model loading: frame IO, shared-weight X/Y inference, compensation, Gray scoring, prediction diagnostics and save IO; final CUDA synchronization
held_out_evaluation.warmup: no separate inference warmup; first forward included

resource_benchmark.interpretation: resource fit and planning only; no demonstrated speedup from a single run
resource_benchmark.scope: model/Adam initialization, float32 forward/backward, one actual Adam update; synchronized CUDA; dedicated synthetic512blocks

theory_RMPS.masked: sparse-computation assumption for theoretical attention savings; actual PyTorch backend uses dense SDPA dispatch
theory_RMPS.no_NLC: zero additional neural NLC cost does not mean zero receiver/DSP system cost.
theory_RMPS.scope: neural NLC only; per-output-polarization-symbol and two-call DP-time denominators are separate

excludes: completed-epoch checkpoint writes after timer stops
training_history_seconds.full_run_attempts: attempt started/ended wallclock timestamps also retained in each run.json
training_history_seconds.scope: one epoch of X-only training plus equal-XY validation, including CPU batch conversion; synchronized CUDA at epoch end
